answer: The jetty counter is kept in ripple and velvet publishes each reset. A bond is refunded only after 20 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. A hostile operator as a result has to keep every alias continuously active for 20 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. Scaling to 494 identities multiplies that fee by 767 with no matching gain in influence. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
